record.paper_title: Ten Conferences WORDS: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: Let X be a finite set of words, and let w be a non-periodic bi-infinite word. Assume that w possesses k disjoint factorizations, with k ≤ |X|. Is it true that we have r(X) ≤ |X| − k + 1?.

evidence.quote: Let X be a finite set of words, and let w be a non-periodic bi-infinite word. Assume that w possesses k disjoint factorizations, with k ≤ |X|. Is it true that we have r(X) ≤ |X| − k + 1?.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X \subseteq \Sigma^+$ be a finite set of nonempty words over a finite alphabet $\Sigma$. The combinatorial rank $r(X)$ of $X$ is defined as
$$r(X) = \min\{\,|F| : F \subseteq \Sigma^+ \text{ and } X \subseteq F^*\,\}.$$
A bi-infinite word over $\Sigma$ is a sequence $w = \cdots a_{-1}a_0 a_1 \cdots \in \Sigma^{\mathbb{Z}}$, and $w$ is called non-periodic if there is no positive integer $p$ with $a_{i+p}=a_i$ for all $i\in\mathbb{Z}$. An $X$-factorization of $w$ is a factorization of $w$ as a bi-infinite concatenation of elements of $X$, i.e. an increasing bi-infinite sequence of integer cut points $(\ldots < c_{-1} < c_0 < c_1 < \ldots)$ such that for each $i$, the factor $a_{c_i}a_{c_i+1}\cdots a_{c_{i+1}-1}$ belongs to $X$. Two $X$-factorizations are called disjoint if their sets of cut points are disjoint.

Question: Suppose $X$ is a finite set of words and $w$ is a non-periodic bi-infinite word that admits $k$ pairwise disjoint $X$-factorizations, where $k \le |X|$. Is it always true that
$$r(X) \le |X| - k + 1\,?$$
artifact.status_search_result: The cumulative defect effect for bi-infinite words is known only in restricted cases (e.g. when X is a finite prefix set with 3 disjoint factorizations, giving rank ≤ |X|−2), and the two-element case has been studied separately. No source found establishes or refutes the general conjecture for arbitrary k disjoint factorizations, so its current status appears unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Defect Effect of Bi-infinite Words in the Two-element Case
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the two-element case of the defect effect for bi-infinite words, indicating only partial cases are resolved.
status_evidence.claim: Only special cases (|X|=2, prefix sets with 3 disjoint factorizations) of the cumulative defect effect for bi-infinite words are known.

status_evidence.title: A defect theorem for bi-infinite words
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes the basic defect theorem for bi-infinite words: two factorizations imply r(X) ≤ |X|−1.
status_evidence.claim: The basic case k=2 is established; the general k case is the conjectured cumulative defect effect.

status_evidence.title: Cumulative defect
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses rare cases where a cumulative defect effect is known to hold, such as prefix sets with three disjoint factorizations.
status_evidence.claim: General cumulative defect effect for k disjoint factorizations of bi-infinite words remains an open problem.
